How is Illinois organized for a home sale?

Illinois has 102 counties, and nearly every step of a house sale touches a county office. Cook County is the largest, with about 5.19 million residents according to the Wikipedia county list, and it holds Chicago.

That spread matters to a seller. The rules come from state law, but forms, fees and office procedures differ from one county to the next.

We list every county and city we cover further down this page. If you want the state level view first, our Illinois guides by city and county page is a good starting point, and the Illinois property tax guide explains how tax bills are built.

What does a cash sale as-is mean in Illinois?

A cash sale as-is means the buyer pays without a mortgage and takes the house in its current condition. You do not repair, paint or clean to meet a lender's appraisal.

As-is does not erase every duty a seller has. Illinois requires a radon disclosure on most residential sales, covered below, and a title company will still search the property for liens, unpaid taxes and judgments before closing. Your own situation shapes the rest:

  • A house with a mortgage needs a payoff figure from the lender so the sale proceeds can clear the loan.
  • A house with unpaid property tax needs the balance settled at or before closing.
  • An inherited house needs someone with legal authority to sign the deed.
  • A rented house needs a plan for the people living in it.

Ask early who will prepare the deed and the transfer declaration, so nothing waits on paperwork at the end.

How do property taxes and exemptions affect a seller?

Property tax in Illinois is a county and local matter, so the first call is to the office that handles your county's assessments. The Illinois Department of Revenue lists several homestead exemptions that reduce the equalized assessed value of an owner-occupied home. The ones sellers ask about most are below.

ExemptionReduction in equalized assessed valueWho qualifies
General HomesteadUp to $10,000 in Cook County, $8,000 in counties next to Cook, $6,000 elsewhereOwner-occupied residences
Senior Citizens HomesteadUp to $8,000 in Cook and contiguous counties, $5,000 elsewhereOwners age 65 or older
Senior Citizens Assessment FreezeFreezes the base year valueAge 65 or older, income limit $75,000 for tax year 2026
Persons with Disabilities$2,000Primary residence of a person with a disability
Homestead ImprovementUp to $75,000 of added fair cash value for four yearsOwners who improved the home

Filing rules vary by county, and Cook County asks seniors to apply every year. Confirm with your county's chief assessment office what is on your bill.

County offices publish their own guides. Browse the county sections below, or read our Illinois homestead exemption and senior exemption pages.

How does foreclosure work in Illinois?

Illinois foreclosures go through the courts, so a lender must file a case and win a judgment before the house can be sold at a foreclosure sale. For a residential mortgage, state law sets the redemption period at whichever is later: seven months after all borrowers were served with the summons, or three months after the judgment of foreclosure.

The statute shortens that window in two cases. If the court finds the home is worth less than 90 percent of the redemption amount and the lender gives up any deficiency claim, the period can end 60 days after judgment. If the court finds the property abandoned, it can end 30 days after judgment.

  • An owner who plans to redeem must send written notice to the lender's attorney at least 15 days before the redemption date, not counting weekends and court holidays.
  • Once the redemption right expires, it does not come back.
  • Selling the house for cash before the deadline can pay the lender from the proceeds, if the payoff covers the judgment amount.

Cook County homeowners who received a court summons can call the Chancery Division's mediation helpline at (855) 452-2637 for a free meeting with a housing counselor. Owners with no summons yet can call Cook County Legal Aid for Housing and Debt at (855) 956-5763. In other counties, ask the circuit clerk what help exists. Our Illinois foreclosure process guide goes into more detail.

What happens when property taxes go unpaid?

Counties sell delinquent property tax at tax sales, and the buyer receives a certificate. The owner can redeem the property by paying what is owed within a set period. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-350, that period is three years from the date of sale for most property.

Shorter periods apply to vacant non-farm property, buildings with seven or more residential units and commercial or industrial property, which can be redeemed within one year. Amendments effective January 1, 2024 and July 10, 2026 apply to certificates issued on or after those dates, so check your certificate's issue date before you rely on a number. See our Illinois tax sales page and ask the county collector for the exact redemption amount.

How does an inherited house get sold in Illinois?

A buyer and a title company need to see who has authority to sign the deed. That might be an executor or administrator appointed through the probate court, or heirs who hold title another way. Which path applies depends on the will, the deed and the estate.

The Illinois small estate affidavit is often mentioned here, and it has a narrow scope. The statute, 755 ILCS 5/25-1, lets people collect personal property when no letters of office are outstanding and the personal estate, not counting registered vehicles, does not exceed $150,000. The text speaks of personal property such as bank accounts and stock, and it does not address real estate. A probate attorney or the circuit clerk in the decedent's county can say whether a house needs a court case.

For more, read our probate process, small estate affidavit and inheritance tax guides.

What transfer tax and recording steps come with a sale?

Illinois charges a state transfer tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the transfer declaration. If the deed says the property is transferred subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage amount drops out of the tax base. The tax is due whether or not the deed is recorded.

ItemWhat the sources say
State transfer tax rate50 cents per $500 of value or fraction
Declaration formPTAX-203, filed with the deed or within 3 business days of the transfer
Electronic filingMyDec in participating counties; paper or fill-in forms elsewhere
ChicagoCity of Chicago Form 7551 is handled through MyDec
Where deeds are recordedThe county recorder of deeds

Some counties and cities add their own transfer tax on top of the state tax, and we did not confirm those rates on official pages for every county. Ask the recorder before closing. Our Illinois transfer tax and quitclaim deed pages have more.

Can I sell a house that has tenants?

Yes, and the buyer will want to know the lease terms. Illinois eviction law sets minimum notice periods that affect timing:

  • For unpaid rent, a landlord may serve a written demand giving the tenant at least 5 days to pay, after which the lease can be ended and an eviction case filed.
  • For a week to week tenant who holds over, a written 7 day notice ends the tenancy.
  • For other tenancies shorter than one year, the notice is 30 days in writing.

Chicago has added a pilot Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act for certain areas, so a Chicago owner of a rented building should ask the city before listing. Our Illinois eviction process page covers the steps in order.

What property issues do Illinois sellers face?

Radon is the one with a legal disclosure attached. Under the Illinois Radon Awareness Act, a seller of residential property with one to four units must give the buyer the state radon pamphlet and a disclosure form before the buyer is bound to a contract. The Act does not require the seller to test or fix anything. It does require the seller to pass along any test results in hand.

Transfers by an estate fiduciary, by succession and after foreclosure are excluded. We did not source flood or well and septic rules for this page, so ask your county health department or recorder about local requirements.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Illinois have?

Illinois has 102 counties. Forms and fees vary by county.

Can I sell my house while it is in foreclosure?

Yes. A sale that closes before redemption ends can pay the lender from proceeds. Ask the lender for a payoff figure.

What is the Illinois state transfer tax?

The state tax is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction. Your county or city may add its own tax.

Do I have to test for radon before selling?

No. You must give the buyer the radon pamphlet and disclosure form and share any results you have. Testing is not required.

Does the small estate affidavit cover a house?

The statute addresses personal property up to $150,000 and does not mention real estate. Ask a probate attorney whether your house needs a court case.

How long do I have to redeem after a tax sale?

Three years from the sale date for most property, and one year for vacant non-farm, commercial, industrial and 7 or more unit buildings. Check your certificate's issue date.

How much notice must I give a tenant who owes rent?

A written demand must give at least 5 days to pay. If the tenant does not, the landlord may start an eviction case without further notice.

Which office do I call about my property tax bill?

Start with your county's chief assessment office. The county sections below link to our tax guides.
